record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For supervised machine-learning algorithms built from matrix product states or related tensor networks, can one express the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension explicitly as a function of the bond dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider supervised machine-learning models whose hypothesis classes are parameterized by tensor networks of fixed topology — in particular, matrix product states (MPS). Recall that an MPS on N sites with bond dimension D and local physical dimension d is a tensor

  T_{s_1 s_2 ... s_N} = Tr( A^{(1)}_{s_1} A^{(2)}_{s_2} ... A^{(N)}_{s_N} ),

where each A^{(k)}_{s_k} is a D × D matrix (with appropriate boundary conditions) and s_k ∈ {1, ..., d}. Given a feature map x ↦ Φ(x) ∈ (C^d)^{⊗N}, define an MPS-based classifier (or regressor) by

  f_T(x) = ⟨T, Φ(x)⟩,

and let H_{N,d,D} denote the hypothesis class obtained by varying the MPS tensors A^{(k)} subject to a fixed bond dimension D (and, for classification, thresholding f_T).

The task is the following:

(a) Derive an explicit closed-form expression, or matching upper and lower bounds, for the Vapnik–Chervonenkis dimension VC(H_{N,d,D}) as a function of the bond dimension D (and of N, d).

(b) Derive an explicit expression, or matching upper and lower bounds, for the (empirical or worst-case) Rademacher complexity R_m(H_{N,d,D}) of the same class as a function of the bond dimension D, the sample size m, and N, d.

More generally, do the analogous question for hypothesis classes built from other tensor-network families (e.g. tree tensor networks, MERA, PEPS) parameterized by their bond dimensions.
artifact.status_search_result: Upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension (and pseudo-dimension) of tensor-network classifiers, including MPS classifiers as a function of the bond dimension, have been established (Khavari–Rabusseau, arXiv:2106.11827, 2021), yielding generalization bounds. However, fully tight/explicit closed-form expressions for the Rademacher complexity and VC dimension across general tensor-network architectures do not appear to be settled, so the broader question remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Lower and Upper Bounds on the VC-Dimension of Tensor Network Models
status_evidence.snippet: We derive upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension and pseudo-dimension of tensor network models... As a corollary we obtain a bound on the VC dimension of the matrix product state classifier introduced in [Stoudenmire and Schwab, 2016] as a function of the so-called bond dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds on the VC dimension of MPS classifiers as a function of bond dimension have been established, partially answering the question.
